# Part I: Foundations {.unnumbered .part}

Three chapters stand between you and the first project: one for the Publish step of the loop,
one for Prompt and Check, and one for the machine that runs them all.

**Chapter 1, Publishing That Rebuilds Itself.** Why hand-made reports drift out of date, and
how Quarto rebuilds every output from one source so that they cannot. You will follow one
file through the three steps of a render, learn exactly what "reproducible" promises, and see
when Quarto is the wrong tool.

**Chapter 2, Working With a Coding Assistant.** What an assistant is, what it costs, how far
its reach goes, and how to ask it for work you can verify. You will learn to read the
book's hands-on boxes, and how to account for an assistant's use when the work is research.

**Chapter 3, Setting Up Your Machine.** Six steps, each with a check you can see, from an
empty terminal to a working assistant, Quarto and Python. It ends when a web page and a PDF
that your own computer built both say 42.

The first two chapters are mostly reading. The third is hands-on: do it at a desk, with a
good connection and about an hour to spare.
